description: Opt-in overlay for repositories that want to group non-major dependency updates into fewer pull requests. Extend after the default preset.

packageRules.description: Group non-major updates into a single review batch

Webgrip packages pinned in files a repository never ships (CI files and mise.toml) share one branch per repository in every stack that groups updates, majors included. Renovate gives a branch the highest commit type among its updates (fix beats ci), so a branch shared with anything that ships would commit these pins as fix(deps) and cut a release again. Majors join the branch and separateMajorMinor is off for these pins, so each pin moves straight to the newest release: two pins of webgrip/workflows on different majors used to split into a minor in the shared branch and a major of their own, and the second to merge conflicted with the first. Renovate merges a branch only when every update in it merges itself, and a Webgrip major never does, so a branch that holds a major waits for a person. The rule changes only the branch and the major split: whoever merges, the tick and the soak stay as the earlier parts set them. webgrip/workflows ships its CI files, so its pins stay where they were.

Shared preset bumps merge themselves once the pull request checks are green: no dashboard tick, no release-age soak, their own branch. The preset is Webgrip's own reviewed code, released from this repository, and every consumer waiting for a tick on it is a policy fix that has not landed. Renovate's automerge, not the platform's, so a branch without checks does not merge at once. It is never digest-pinned: It is already pinned to a protected semver release tag; the global pinDigests=true otherwise makes Renovate try to rewrite 'local>webgrip/renovate-config#vX.Y.Z' to a commit SHA, the replacement never applies ('Digest is not updated'), and the whole pin-dependencies branch aborts with 'Error updating branch: update failure' on every run. A preset bump changes how Renovate treats the repository, not what it ships, so it lands as chore(renovate) and never cuts a release.. The generator appends this part to every preset it builds, so no grouping, soak or commit-type rule of an earlier part can catch the bump.
